At alpha=1 the original lower bound D^n/(4^n C_H A) is recovered exactly.
The new stability proof keeps competitor bounds, torsion intervals and constants independent of the solution oscillation.

Large errors and zero errors are covered separately, with no division by zero.
Every dominated density retains the same all-Borel capacity constant; the coefficient lower bound follows from actual total clipped mass.
Taking the decreasing scalar limit is legitimate since dominated densities and clips are nonzero integrable data.
The root estimate uses all original tests, including the zero-tail case, rather than a selected family.
Both L^n tails and the root tails vanish, proving membership in the existing closed order ideal.
Almost-everywhere subsequence convergence upgrades to a two-index error against the fixed finite absolutely continuous measure f dV.
The common mass domination and both orders of quantitative stability yield uniform Cauchy potentials.
Uniform limits preserve canonical h-plurisubharmonicity and normalization.
Closed local difference products paired with CLN bounds converge; every signed smooth Hermitian correction factor remains in the expansion.
The product limit equals the L^1 density limit at exactly b_h(f), with a finite strictly positive prescribed mass.
The logarithmic potential extends continuously across the centre and remains h/2-positive after cutoff scaling.
Local capacity domination of all smooth-correction terms rules out an origin atom, giving global absolute continuity.
The exact radial determinant coefficient and ball flux use dd^c=i partial barpartial/(2 pi).
Every lower mixed degree has O(r^2) ball mass; the displayed radial integral proves failure of every higher L^p class.
The volume-capacity split covers all Borel sets, capacity zero and the large-capacity regime.
The explicit datum is bounded below, so its open modified-comparison sets have positive measure.
Modified comparison calibrates b_h(f)=1 while retaining the actual reserve and vanishing torsion factor.
The direct radius K^(-1/(4n)) gives the logarithmic root-tail rate without an implicit inversion.
The local section setting prevents n>=3 from becoming a global hypothesis on later material.
The fixed-datum capacity condition has not been deduced from arbitrary finite root norm or uniform root tails; both unrestricted S04 questions remain open.
